extracted.intended_audience: doctoral students applying to the DOE Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (CSGF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for doctoral applicants deciding which DOE CSGF track to apply to and whether they meet program eligibility; includes track-specific field/department and research-focus requirements related to high-performance computing (HPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Track selection: Science & Engineering Track
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science & Engineering Track accepts doctoral students engaged in computational science research with a science or engineering focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship supports doctoral students in fields of study that advance the use of HPC to solve specific, complex science and engineering problems. These fields span science and technology, ranging from engineering to biological sciences and from astrophysics to geophysics. "Those whose interests and plans match this definition should apply for the Science & Engineering Track."

rubrics_metrics.name: Track selection: Mathematics & Computer Science Track
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mathematics & Computer Science Track accepts students pursuing research in broadly applicable methods and technology for high-performance computing (HPC) systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics and computer science fellows need not focus on a particular science or engineering application, but instead must be developing broadly applicable methods and technology that support computational science using HPC. "Those who fit this description should apply for the Math/CS Track." Additional details and examples of appropriate research areas are available on the Math/CS Track information page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement: doctoral enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be doctoral students (pursuing a doctoral degree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both tracks are described as supporting doctoral students or doctoral candidates; students should be enrolled in a doctoral program to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department/academic affiliation requirement (Math/CS Track)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students applying to the Math/CS Track must be pursuing a doctoral degree in applied mathematics, statistics, computer science, computer engineering or computational science — in one of these departments or their academic equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A departmental exception is made for students whose research is focused on algorithms or software for quantum information systems and who are enrolled in a science or engineering field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required research contribution to HPC
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must contribute to more effective use of emerging HPC systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies across tracks: the Science & Engineering Track emphasizes using HPC to solve specific, complex science/engineering problems; the Math/CS Track emphasizes developing methods/technology that support computational science on HPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of appropriate Math/CS research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Students performing research in computer science, computer engineering, or electrical engineering — including development of novel hardware technology, machine learning or broadly applicable software without a specific science or engineering focus — should apply to the Math/CS Track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, students performing research in applied mathematics or statistics with a focus on broadly applicable methods or technologies without a specific science or engineering focus should also apply to the Math/CS Track. See the Math/CS Track information page for additional examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to review track criteria before applying / contact for questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible fellowship candidates should carefully review the criteria for both tracks prior to initiating the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain which track fits, please contact the program with questions (link provided on the page).
